subject: Renewal discussion: capacity uplift + pricing anchor (Umbra Solutions)
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@umbrasolutions.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion: capacity uplift + pricing anchor (Umbra Solutions)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Umbra's usage trajectory is clear and we want to propose a renewal that preserves price stability while giving you headroom for the expected capacity uplift. High level: we can offer a 12-month price hold on your primary model tier if you commit to a stepped uplift (details below), plus a one-time credit to smooth the first quarter of overage risk.

Quick sketch — please tell me what matters most to you and I’ll convert this to a formal term sheet:
- Baseline: maintain current unit price for first 12 months if Umbra commits to 1.3x current committed tokens over the next 12 months.
- Credit: $50,000 one-time credit applied to Q1 invoice to cover onboarding/overage while traffic ramps.
- Burst: short-term burst capacity (auto-bill above commit) with capped overage rate for 90 days.

I attached a short RFP reference you mentioned (for our ops and pricing alignment). Can we schedule a 30-minute follow-up tomorrow to review?

Best,
David Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
-- Attachment: UMBRA_RFP.pdf (pdf, 520KB)
From: Elena Rossi <elena@umbrasolutions.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@umbrasolutions.com
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: capacity uplift + pricing anchor (Umbra Solutions)

David —

Thanks for the quick outline. That aligns directionally. Two asks from our side before a formal term sheet: 1) a firmer pricehold (12 months is good but we want the option to extend a locked unit price for 18 months if we commit to a larger uplift), and 2) the one-time credit looks helpful but can you show a scenario with credits tiered by achieved ramp (e.g., $50k if you hit 80% of uplift in Q1, $25k if 60%). Procurement copied — Marco will coordinate approvals and needs a draft MAPl (mutual action plan) plus an itemized TCO.

Can you also include an itemized note on how KV-cache and prefix caching will be handled for our multi-service routing? That is a gating technical ask for our infra team.

Elena
VP, Platform — Umbra Solutions
-- Attachment: (from us) UMBRA_RFP.pdf referenced
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@umbrasolutions.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: capacity uplift + pricing anchor (Umbra Solutions)

Elena / Marco —

Appreciate the clarity. Attached is a concise term sheet draft and a pricing model workbook with the tiered-credit scenarios you asked for. High-level options so we can converge quickly:

Option A (Aggressive uplift)
- Commit: 1.5x current committed tokens for 18 months
- Price: current unit rate held for 18 months
- Credit: $75k tiered ($75k if 90% ramp in Q1; $50k at 80%; $25k at 60%)
- Burst cap: 90-day capped overage at 1.2x base rate

Option B (Conservative)
- Commit: 1.25x current committed tokens for 12 months
- Price: current unit rate held for 12 months
- Credit: $40k one-time (prorated by ramp)
- Burst cap: standard overage rates, no temporary cap

Technical note: Marissa, Monica — below is the short description on caching/routing Elena requested that we can expand for the MAP:
- KV/prefix caching: we’ll pin the most frequent prefixes to a low-latency pool and enable cross-service KV sharing; caching invalidation window set to 30s by default with an ops-runbook for fast rollbacks.

Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_v1.pdf (term sheet), renewal_pricing_model.xlsx (scenario workbook). If you can mark a preferred option and confirm preferred timeline (12 vs 18 months), we’ll route to legal and prepare a DocuSign.

Thanks —
David
-- Attachments: redwood_term_sheet_v1.pdf (pdf, 210KB); renewal_pricing_model.xlsx (xlsx, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion: capacity uplift + pricing anchor (Umbra Solutions)

Team —

Good framing. A few internal points before we send a final to Umbra:
1) Finance/legal will need a clean walk-through of the tiered-credit triggers (we should table the $75k top level until finance confirms liability treatment).
2) I can approve a 10% additional concession on the base list price to secure the 18-month anchor, + recommend a $30k guaranteed credit (with the remaining credit contingent on ramp milestones). That preserves some upside while limiting immediate credit exposure.
3) Ops to validate the caching plan and confirm SLA impact; Monica, can you draft a short ops note and an acceptance checklist?

If everyone aligns, I’ll prepare a short internal approval note for Kathy in Legal and Luke in Finance and then we can populate the DocuSign envelope.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
-- Attachment stub: internal_approval_checklist.md (md)
